brief: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says the correction that began in June is in its final stages but needs three 'clearing events' before a low: an AI funding glut, the midterm elections, and a Fed liquidity squeeze. Markets must absorb a wave of AI-related capital raises and credit supply (Meta's up to $95bn equity raise, Broadcom's financing warning) before semis bottom roughly 10-15% lower by mid-November, SOX near 9,500, which Wilson expects to coincide with funding concerns easing. Next Tuesday's midterms are historically bullish (S&P up 14.8%/16.6% six/twelve months after every midterm since 1950), but the larger overhang is a potential post-election Iran escalation the administration has floated; Wilson says such shocks have often been short-term buying opportunities and could trigger the final capitulation. Third, Fed chair Warsh has slowed balance-sheet growth by half, tightening financial conditions on par with 2018; liquidity must worsen before the Fed adds it back, marking the low. Wilson's tactical S&P downside target is 7100-7200, roughly 6-7% below 7,624, before a rally to his 8000 year-end and 8300 12-month base cases. Sentiment remains neutral, not capitulated; retail is still buying semis with 3x leverage even as hedge funds reversed AI net buying.
